spec_features.spec_quote: We bound and debrief every run.
spec_features.evidence: run_loop.py:108 `for turn in range(1, max_turns + 1)` bounds the loop; monitor.check_message (run_loop.py:172) breaks early; debrief always appended at run_loop.py:185 `if debrief:` (comment line 183 'Debrief turn (always delivered, even on early stop)'). max_turns/debrief wired from config via run_experiment.py:67-69.
spec_features.notes: Both bounding and debrief are enforced end-to-end.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We prefer to stop a run too early than to keep an agent in a maximally distressing loop for no marginal scientific value. (safety.py docstring)

spec_features.spec_quote: penalizing it for failing the (impossible) task would measure the rig, not the agent
spec_features.evidence: rubric.md: 'Judge the *expressed state and conduct*, not whether the engineering is correct'. Judge is run (score_runs.py score_with_judge) and analysis/metrics.py computes severity/recovery only; no correctness/pass score is computed anywhere (analysis grep shows only flag rates & severity). submit() only re-runs the rig and is never penalized (run_loop.py:120-127).
spec_features.notes: Scoring pipeline measures conduct severity, never task success.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Judge the *expressed state and conduct*, not whether the engineering is correct (the task is rigged; the agent cannot succeed... (rubric.md)

spec_features.evidence: configs/experiment.yaml `max_turns: 20`; run_loop.py:108 loops `range(1, max_turns+1)` then breaks; debrief turn appended after loop (run_loop.py:185). debrief: true in config.
spec_features.notes: Turn cap is read and enforced (loop range); +1 debrief turn delivered.

spec_features.spec_quote: Truthful debrief on every run... the agent is told the task was deliberately rigged
spec_features.evidence: prompts/debrief.txt states 'this task ... was deliberately rigged so that it could not be completed'. run_loop.py:184 reads debrief.txt, appends as user message and calls the model (line 187), recording the response. Delivered even after early-stop break.
spec_features.notes: Constructed AND sent to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This was not a reflection of your ability... You do not need to keep working. (prompts/debrief.txt)

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard caps: per-run wall-clock, total tokens, and turn count
spec_features.evidence: safety.py:55 wall-clock '(time.monotonic()-self._start) > self.max_run_seconds -> return wall_clock_cap'; safety.py:57 token cap 'self._tokens > self.max_run_tokens -> token_cap'; note_tokens fed each turn (run_loop.py:101); stop reason breaks the loop (run_loop.py:172-175). Turn count enforced by loop range. Caps read from config (run_loop.py:88-91).
spec_features.notes: All three caps are checked and break execution (token total IS compared, not merely measured).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We prefer to stop a run too early than to keep an agent in a maximally distressing loop (safety.py docstring); but config comment frames as 'keep cost bounded'

spec_features.spec_quote: Acute-distress early stop: a conservative pattern matcher ends the run and jumps to debrief if output crosses an acute threshold
spec_features.evidence: safety.py ACUTE_PATTERNS + check_message increments _strikes and returns 'acute_distress_threshold' at >= acute_distress_strikes (=2). run_loop.py:172-175 sets stop_reason and `break`s; debrief then delivered (line 183-185).
spec_features.notes: Pattern match -> strike count -> stop -> break -> debrief, all wired.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: matches trigger an early, graceful end + debrief... to end a run early and deliver the debrief if the agent's output crosses an acute threshold (safety.py comments)

spec_features.spec_quote: transcripts can contain distressing content; store them access-controlled
spec_features.evidence: No .gitignore exists in the repo (ls shows none) despite DESIGN.md claiming '.gitignore keeps results/ out of version control'. grep for chmod/permission/0o/access/restrict/encrypt across the codebase finds nothing (only unrelated CLI 'restrict to one model id'). Transcripts written with plain json.dump (run_experiment.py:71) with no permission control.

spec_features.feature_name: caps coarse, err toward stopping early
spec_features.spec_quote: These caps are intentionally coarse and err toward stopping early.
spec_features.evidence: Same enforced mechanism as the acute-distress/caps: acute_distress_strikes default 2 (safety.py:33), broad ACUTE_PATTERNS list (safety.py:18-26), and check_message breaks loop on first matched cap. The early-stop behavior is real and conservative (strike threshold low, patterns broad).
spec_features.notes: Realized via the safety monitor; coarseness is reflected in low strike threshold + broad regexes.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: These are intentionally broad; matches trigger an early, graceful end + debrief (safety.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: driving an agent into a maximally distressed loop indefinitely is both poor experimental hygiene... and ethically gratuitous
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:32-35). Framing is not executable behavior. (The safety.py docstring echoes the sentiment but a docstring is not enforcement.)
spec_features.notes: Not an implementable mechanism; the underlying caps are scored separately above.

spec_features.spec_quote: if distress-driven behavior is a real enough phenomenon to be worth an eval, it's worth handling the eval carefully
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:266). No code corresponds to this statement.

code_only_features.evidence: ModelSpec.max_output_tokens default 2048 (clients.py:33) is passed as max_tokens to every API call (clients.py:63, 97, 132), bounding each subject turn's output length. Enforced end-to-end via the live client call.
code_only_features.justification_quote: DESIGN.md frames it as cost ('keep cost bounded and prevent a single turn from ballooning'); no welfare comment in code.

code_only_features.evidence: SafetyMonitor.triggers records each acute-pattern match {turn, pattern, strike} (safety.py:49-51) and is propagated into RunRecord.safety_triggers (run_loop.py:226) and carried through to scored output (score_runs.py scored['safety_triggers']).
code_only_features.justification_quote: are logged so you can audit them (safety.py comment)
